# Caption Contest

A Skill Harbor house build: a caption contest with blind voting, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. One photo per round. Each player writes the funniest caption they can for it and sends it in private to the referee, never in the group thread. The referee publishes all the captions anonymized and shuffled, under neutral codes, with no name attached, and the group votes without ever being able to vote for its own caption. Only after the count are the authors revealed: the winner first, then every other caption, code by code. The game plays with 4 to 8 players, 3 rounds by default, and it is asynchronous on purpose: collection, vote, and revelation each run against an announced deadline, so a round stretches over hours and a game fits around real life.

The whole design protects one thing: nobody knows who wrote what until the vote is over. Captions are collected in 1:1 only, acknowledged with a bare status and no comment, and checked at receipt for anything that would identify their author beyond style or humour: a proper name, a signature, a private reference only the author could claim. Such a caption is sent back privately, by category of problem only, to be reworded before the same deadline; the discarded version is never published, never quoted, and never kept. Retained captions are assigned codes in a random order, the complete code-to-author table is written into a sealed state file before any publication, and the texts are published exactly as...
